 Aston Villa vs. Viking - Head-to-head record
 Aston Villa and Viking will face each other for the first time in a competitive match. With no previous results between the clubs to analyse, their current form and recent Champions League results offer the clearest indications of what to expect.
 Villa have established themselves as a formidable force at home in Europe, while Viking have shown they can trouble elite opposition after holding Bayern Munich to a draw.
 Aston Villa have scored freely in recent weeks and will test the Norwegian side’s defensive record away from home.

 Aston Villa - In formidable European form
 Fresh from some impressive results, Aston Villa enter this Champions League clash with plenty of confidence. In this section, we’ll delve into their recent performances and tactical setup. We will also preview the likely Aston Villa vs. Viking line-ups for this crucial European night.
 Recent form
 Villa began their European campaign with a 3-2 victory away to Club Brugge before recording their biggest-ever European win, beating Fenerbahce 6-0 at Villa Park. Those results have put them among the teams with a perfect record after two league-phase matches.
 Their domestic form has also improved following a difficult start to the Premier League season. Villa have won five of their last seven matches across all competitions. Their latest result was a 1-0 victory away to Newcastle United, secured by Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.
 Villa also boast an impressive European home record, having gone 14 matches unbeaten at Villa Park in continental competition. They have scored in 22 of their last 23 European matches and netted at least three goals in six of their last eight.
 However, Emery will have several absentees to manage. Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Ian Maatsen, Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Modo Cisse are sidelined, while Manzambi is also ruled out after picking up a knock. Taylor Harwood-Bellis is ineligible for the Champions League.

 Viking - On an impressive streak
 Now, let’s look at Viking. We will analyse their current form, recent results, and the players who could make a difference in this upcoming match.
 Recent form
 Viking have lost only once in their last 12 matches across all competitions, winning eight and drawing three. They remain firmly in the Eliteserien title race, level on points with Bodo/Glimt with seven matches remaining.
 In Europe, they have collected just one point from their opening two fixtures. After losing 3-1 away to Stuttgart, Viking produced an entertaining 3-3 draw against Bayern Munich . They surrendered a two-goal lead and subsequently fell behind, but a 90th-minute equaliser earned them a valuable point.
 Zlatko Tripić has been particularly influential in Europe, with one goal and two assists in Viking’s opening two Champions League matches. Peter Christiansen, the club’s leading scorer, will also be an important attacking threat.
 The visitors also have several injury concerns, as Martin Ove Roseth, Nick D’Agostino, Veton Berisha and Anders Bærtelsen remain unavailable.

 Predictions for Aston Villa vs. Viking - Goals Expected at Villa Park
 Aston Villa’s impressive home record in Europe makes Aston Villa winning at half-time an appealing option. Emery’s side scored six goals against Fenerbahçe in their previous home fixture and will look to establish control early.
 Viking have also shown considerable attacking potential, scoring three times against Bayern Munich. With both teams capable of creating chances, Over 1.5 goals in the first half is another market to consider.
 Our main prediction is Aston Villa to win and over 2.5 goals scored . Villa’s attacking form and strong European home record make them favourites, while Viking’s recent results suggest they could contribute to an entertaining contest.
